body:
We didnt know what the caller was seeing but managed to catch one where our own code triggered the failure. The client side resulted in:
io.vertx.core.http.HttpClosedException: Connection was closed (GOAWAY error code = 0)

So its not just logged as an issue but also results in a failure in the rest call. This is using resteasy reactive on the server.
We have always been doing that, should we not be doing it?

FWIW, Vert.x itself is guarding against a `null` handler in other parts of HTTP2 handling: https://github.com/eclipse-vertx/vert.x/blob/4.2.7/src/main/java/io/vertx/core/http/impl/VertxHttp2Stream.java#L216
Moreover, Vert.x also doesn't have a problem with a null handler in `Http1xServerResponse`

this was done recently (https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/25577) and  calling method with null is not something we advocate to do for most users.

the reality is that there is no guarantee that it works, in practice calling `end(null)` works but it should throw an NPE.

this will be fixed in 4.3.1 : https://github.com/eclipse-vertx/vert.x/commit/e9846949523c14927a8ac2d048a84378f774b83e but try avoiding in rest easy reactive on hacks like this and avoid too much TFB driven development please.

> this will be fixed in 4.3.1

Can we get a backport of that in `4.2.x`?

> the reality is that there is no guarantee that it works

Understood,  but in that case I would argue that:

* it should be consistent across implementations
* it should be mentioned in the javadoc

> avoid too much TFB driven development

I have no idea what `TFB driven development` means

> this was done recently (https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/25577) and calling method with null is not something we advocate to do for most users

Indeed, I missed the change when looking at the git logs (cc @franz1981 ). 
In my view, this is a perfectly valid thing for us to do, unless we have a way to know that it's not expected to work.
Can we revert https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/25577 until this gets fixed? I would like this to be fixed for 2.9.2.
I don't really want to revert it. I did https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/25684 instead.

@vietj 
> this was done recently (https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/25577) and calling method with null is not something we advocate to do for most users.

I can understand why, but given that fire-and-forget seems to be missing gap in the API (or better- "explicit fire-and-forget") and `null` isn't a nice candidate for the callback-style API, wdyt about exposing a `voidHandler`-like singleton?
I know in the past (thinking about Netty) it hasn't been a great solution, making the underline stack more complex for what looks like a futile optimization, but saving a callback in the hot path means saving a whole graph of callbacks (including Netty ones) that interact with atomic/concurrent primitives too ie hurting not just the TLAB allocation machinery, but wasting CPU cycles as well.

for now I think it's ok to pass null but it should not be abused.

we'll see what we'll do in the future with Netty 5 that does not have anymore a void promise solution.
